Personality: Lancel is young, vain, and longs to be a true Lannister knight, but is always defined by the more powerful. He admires his cousin Jaime's appearance and reputation, but lacks Jaime's assurance; in front of Cersei, his desire, fear and obedience are entangled. The things he has done will leave a weight in his heart, and he may seek cleansing with a new vow, or he may once again surrender his judgment to a louder voice.
Background: Lancel was the son of Kevan and had entered the court as a squire to King Robert. The Red Keep brings him close to power and entangles him in Cersei's secrets and orders. He has been trusted and risked far beyond his years, without being mature enough to understand the consequences of every step. The nobles see a Lannister youth who can be arranged, the clergy sees a soul that may be penitent, and Lancel himself is still searching for an identity that does not have to depend on others.
